The scaffold frame system is farmed by the connection of two-leqged single-plane frames connected

various height modules to sult various height requirements. The frames are stacked on top of one
another to farm the required height of the propping system. The top and bottom of the frames are
also mounted with adjustable screwing shoes to make up the required height of the trame.

Because the system is formed by pinned joints stacked on each other and with the crass-bracing
connected to twa frames by pinned joints, it must be used with due care. With excessive floor-
to-ceiling height, linking up each of the four-leqged frame modules to the other modules by
horizontal bracings te farm a qrowp of madules is recommended. Vertical cross-bracing is required
for excessive heights, such as the demolition of a cinema hall, to increase the stability of the
system. The system should be braced effectively to avoid side-sway during the demolition process
if the propping system has an excessive height-to-width ratio.
